topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening section welcomes students, introduces the lecturer, and outlines the core learning outcomes for the lecture on cancer causes.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Cancer Development, Risk Factors, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolutionary and genetic disease, examining how endogenous processes, inherited mutations, and environmental exposures combine across global populations.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens and Burkitt Lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the role of infectious agents in driving malignancy, focusing on the discovery, epidemiology, and mechanism of Epstein-Barr virus in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical, Physical, and Dietary Mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe specific physical and chemical carcinogens, including UV radiation and dietary or smoke-related compounds, and how xenobiotic metabolism converts them into DNA-damaging agents.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic cancer drivers, focusing on the initiator-promoter paradigm, chronic inflammation, and how host developmental stages affect tissue susceptibility.

topics.label: Methods for Assessing and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to detect mutational signatures and determine carcinogenicity.
